test_title: PYST 27: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following was a tribal rebellion led by Birsa, a leader from Ranchi, that began as a religious movement and later turned into a fight against colonial land settlement, moneylenders and forest contractors?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Munda uprising**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Munda uprising** was a tribal rebellion led by **Birsa Munda**, a revered tribal leader from the region of **Ranchi** in present-day Jharkhand.
 
• The rebellion began as a **religious movement** in the late 19th century and later evolved into a struggle against colonial policies, specifically those concerning **land settlement, moneylenders, and forest contractors**.
 
• Birsa Munda, also known as **Dharti Abba** (Father of the Earth), mobilized the Munda tribal community to fight against the **oppressive British administration** and the exploitative practices of landlords and moneylenders.
 
• The rebellion was aimed at reclaiming the rights of the tribal people to their land and resources, which were being seized under the British **Zamindari system**.
 
• Though the uprising was eventually suppressed by the British in **1900**, it played a crucial role in inspiring tribal resistance movements and contributed to the **tribal identity and independence struggle** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Birsa Munda:**

 
 
• He was born on **15 November 1875** in Ulihatu, now in Jharkhand.
 
• Birsa Munda envisioned a golden age called **“Ulgulan”** or the Great Rebellion, where tribals would live in harmony, free from oppression.
 
• He emphasized the importance of tribal identity and culture while rejecting the exploitative practices of the colonial and feudal systems.
 
 
 
• **Causes of Munda Rebellion:**
 
 
• The introduction of the **Zamindari system** by the British led to the loss of traditional tribal lands.
 
• Moneylenders, landlords, and forest contractors exploited the Munda community, leading to extreme poverty and injustice.
 
• The erosion of tribal customs and culture due to the influence of missionaries and colonial administration further fueled discontent.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Munda Uprising:**
 
 
• Though short-lived, the rebellion highlighted the plight of tribal communities under the British regime.
 
• Birsa Munda became a symbol of **tribal resistance and empowerment**, and his contributions are celebrated to this day.
 
• The state of Jharkhand recognizes his legacy, and **15 November** is celebrated as **“Birsa Munda Jayanti”**.
 
 
 
• **Details of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Kuka Rebellion:** It was a Sikh uprising against British colonial rule, led by the Namdhari sect in Punjab during the 1870s.
 
• **Sannyasi Revolt:** This revolt occurred in Bengal in the late 18th century, where Sannyasis (Hindu ascetics) fought against the British due to religious restrictions and economic exploitation.
 
• **Wahabi Movement:** A revivalist Islamic movement in India during the 19th century, aimed at purifying Islam and resisting British colonial influence.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Significance:** The Munda Rebellion was among the most significant tribal uprisings in colonial India, demonstrating the agency and resistance of indigenous communities against systemic oppression.
 
• **Birsa Munda's Death:** He died on **9 June 1900** in Ranchi Jail under mysterious circumstances, making him a martyr for the tribal cause.
 
• **Impact on Tribal Policies:** The uprising forced the British to introduce the **Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908**, which aimed to protect tribal lands from being transferred to non-tribals.
 
• **Recognition:** Birsa Munda is commemorated across India, especially in tribal-dominated regions, as a freedom fighter and social reformer.
